 ORDER
This common order shall govern disposal of MA No.1210/2015 & MA No.1211/2015 as both the appeals arise out of a common award arising out of the same accident.

2. Both these appeals have been filed by the insurance company under section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act arising out of the award dated 06.05.2015 passed by 3rd MACT, Indore in claim case no.20/15 & 21/15 seeking exoneration from liability to pay compensation.
3. The date of accident and negligence are not in dispute in these appeals and the findings recorded by the Tribunal in this regard are also not in question.

As per the findings of the Tribunal, for the death of Kalu @ Karan the Tribunal has awarded a compensation of Rs.5,11,000/- in claim case no.21/15 and for the injuries sustained by the claimant Ambaram, awarded a compensation of Rs.10,500/- in claim case no.20/15 along with interest from the date of claim petition till its realization.
4.
The insurance company has filed these appeals on the ground that the deceased and injured were gratuitous passengers at the time of accident in the offending vehicle.
They were not sitting in the cabin of the vehicle at the time of accident, therefore, the insurance company is not liable to pay the compensation.
The Tribunal has committed error in fastening the liability to pay compensation on the insurance company.

sentences.text: 5. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent/claimants has supported the impugned award and prayed for dismissal of the appeals.

6. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
7.
Undisputedly, the deceased Kalu as well as injured Ambaram were travelling in the offending vehicle at the time of accident along with the goods but they were not sitting in the cabin.

8. In the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Cholleti Bharatamma and others - 2008 ACJ 268,
the apex Court has held in para- 17 & 18 as under:
17.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Cholleti Bharatamma and others - 2008 ACJ 268
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is not well settled that the owner of the goods means only the person who travels in the cabin of the vehicle.
18. In this case, the High Court had proceeded on the basis that they were gratuitous passengers.
The admitted plea of the respondents themselves was that the deceased had boarded the lorry and paid an amount of Rs.20 as transport charges.
It has not been proved that the deceased was travelling in the lorry along with the driver or the cleaner as the owner of the goods.
Travelling with the goods itself does not entitle anyone to the protection under section 147 of the Motor Vehicles Act.

9. The coordinate Bench of this Court in the case of Shriram General Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Smt.Kshama Kahar (MA No.1117/2021 decided on 11.05.2023) has held that the vehicle with the person sitting on the loading part of the vehicle without any resistance clearly indicates that deceased was permitted by the driver for sitting on the loading vehicle, therefore, it can be a violation of the terms and conditions of the insurance policy by the insured for which the injured or deceased cannot be held liable.

entities.text: Shriram General Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Smt.Kshama Kahar (MA No.1117/2021 decided
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the present case, perusal of the record of the Tribunal it is found that at the time of accident the deceased and claimant injured were sitting on the loading part of the vehicle with their goods and they were not sitting in the cabin.

So, it is clearly established that the driver and owner of the offending vehicle violated the terms and conditions of the insurance policy, therefore, the insurance company is exonerated from its liability but relying upon the verdict in the case of Shriram General Insurance Co. vs. Sm.Kshama Kahar (supra), the insurance company shall pay the compensation amount with liberty to recover the same from the owner and driver of the vehicle.

entities.text: Shriram General Insurance Co. vs. Sm.Kshama Kahar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 10. Accordingly, the appeals are allowed in part with the aforesaid modification in the impugned award.

(HIRDESH) JUDGE hk/
